sample.name: Museum of American Heritage
facts: A history of technology museum in the 1907 Williams house, designed by Ernest Coxhead.
Rhona Williams left the home and garden to Palo Alto in 1989 for cultural use.
Founded in 1990

sample.name: San Jose Museum of Quilts & Textiles
facts: Founded in 1977 by members of the Santa Clara Valley Quilt Association.
Described as the first museum in the United States to focus solely on quilts and textiles.
Bought its 13,000 square foot SoFA building in 2005 in partnership with the City of San Jose.

sample.name: Movimiento de Arte y Cultura Latino Americana
facts: Founded in 1989 out of a community mobilization on behalf of multicultural arts.
Contemporary arts space grounded in the Chicano and Latino experience.
Founded in 1989

sample.name: Lucy Evans Baylands Nature Interpretive Center
facts: Occupies an A-frame barn built by Dr. Russel V. Lee, who bought the land in 1941.
Sits within the 1,940-acre Baylands Nature Preserve.
Run by City of Palo Alto's Open Space, Parks and Golf Administration

sample.name: Works/San José
facts: Began in October 1977 as a group of artists and San Jose State University faculty and students.
Has presented performance art, music, film, theater, spoken word and visual art.
Founded in 1977

sample.name: Triton Museum of Art
facts: Founded in 1965 by rancher and lawyer W. Robert Morgan and his wife June.
It was the first non-university art museum in Santa Clara County.
The current building was completed in October 1987.

sample.name: Sunnyvale Heritage Park Museum
facts: The museum building is a replica of Martin Murphy Jr.'s Bay View Ranch house.
The museum opened in September 2008.
Founded in 2008

sample.name: Institute of Contemporary Art San José
facts: Artists incorporated it in October 1980, and its first exhibition opened October 19, 1980.
Bought its 7,500-square-foot building in the SoFA district in April 2006.
Founded in 1980

sample.name: Anno Domini Gallery
facts: Started by graphic designers Cherri Lakey and Brian Eder.
Shows street art, zine culture and tattoo art by emerging and international artists.
Address: 366 South 1st Street, San Jose

sample.name: Pacific Art League
facts: Founded in 1921 as the Palo Alto Art Club.
Has owned its Birge Clark designed Spanish Revival building since 1965.
Address: 668 Ramona Street, Palo Alto

sample.name: Palo Alto Art Center
facts: Runs Project Look, a school tour program in its contemporary art gallery.
Keeps an archive of its exhibitions dating back to 1971.
Run by City of Palo Alto
